title: Modeling light-matter coupled systems with neural quantum states
authors: Noe Salmeron, Marin Bukov, Markus Schmitt
abstract: Recent advances in cold atom manipulation enable the study of many-body systems where short-range interactions between neighboring atoms coexist with long-range interactions mediated by photons. Such a combination of interactions makes a theoretical approach challenging beyond mean-field methods. In this work, we develop a neural quantum state based approach to study these systems numerically. We introduce a neural-network architecture capable of handling hybrid Hilbert spaces with large local bosonic dimensions in strongly interacting spin-photon systems. We benchmark this approach on a model of a two-dimensional lattice of Rydberg atoms coupled to a photon mode. The superradiant ground states found in the large spin-photon coupling regime allow us to demonstrate the efficiency of the method in the presence of high photon occupation. Furthermore, the ability to capture spin-spin and spin-photon correlations leads us to observe quantitative deviations in the ground state phase boundaries with respect to mean-field theory. The method extends to other systems with a similar hybrid Hilbert space structure, such as spin-phonon systems, and provides a scalable framework for investigating their ground state properties.
summary: The paper introduces and validates Neural Quantum States (NQS) as a powerful numerical technique to simulate light-matter coupled quantum systems. It models Rydberg atoms interacting with cavity photons, accurately predicting ground state phase boundaries by capturing crucial spin-photon correlations missed by mean-field theory. This method offers a scalable framework for studying complex strongly correlated physics in hybrid quantum platforms.
main_problem: Developing a robust numerical method to study complex many-body quantum systems where short-range interactions coexist with long-range photon-mediated couplings, exceeding the capabilities of mean-field theory.
main_result: The Neural Quantum State (NQS) approach successfully captures spin-photon and spin-spin correlations, leading to quantitative deviations in predicted ground state phase boundaries compared to mean-field calculations.
method: The study employs Neural Quantum States (NQS), utilizing a multi-head ResNet architecture to represent the wavefunction on hybrid Hilbert spaces. A unitary transformation is used to map the system to a stoquastic Hamiltonian, enabling Variational Monte Carlo optimization.
model_or_system: The model is a light-matter coupled system, specifically a 2D lattice of Rydberg atoms interacting with a cavity photon mode (spin-photon coupling). The Hamiltonian includes spin interactions ($H_{	ext{spin}}$), cavity terms ($H_{	ext{cavity}}$), and the interaction term ($H_{	ext{int}}$).
key_observables: Ground state properties, phase boundaries (FP, AFM, SR phases), Renyi-2 entanglement entropy, and energy expectation values.
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ratios like $g/\Delta$ and $V/\Delta$; photon cutoff ($n_{	ext{cutoff}}$); system size ($N$).
main_assumptions: The method requires truncating the infinite photon degree of freedom at a finite cutoff ($n_{	ext{cutoff}}$) and assumes adiabatic preparation for ground state calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing predicted boundaries, comparison plots between NQS and mean-field results for order parameters (AFM/SR), and convergence diagnostics like energy variance vs. time step or cutoff size.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing the physical model and Hamiltonian, detailing the necessary unitary transformation to ensure stochasticity, presenting the advanced multi-head ResNet NQS architecture, validating its stability through initialization techniques, and finally applying it to map out phase diagrams and quantify correlation effects beyond mean-field theory.
why_interesting: This work represents a significant advancement in simulating strongly correlated quantum systems by providing a scalable, highly accurate numerical tool (NQS) that surpasses the limitations of traditional methods like Mean-Field Theory or Tensor Networks for specific hybrid Hilbert spaces.

They are additionally uniformly coupled to a single cavity photon mode with interaction strength g. The cavity effectively mediates an all-to-all coupling competing with the nearest-neighbor interaction. An external field with intensity ∆is also present. For electrically neutral Rydberg atoms, this field can take the form of an external periodic drive [1]. FIG. 2. Schematic illustration of the neural network architecture. We adapt the ResNet architecture previously used for spin-only systems [24]. A spin configuration is given as input and passes through multiple convolutional layers with residual connections. Our modification occurs at the end of these layers: instead of averaging all feature maps to a single number, we average each one separately to produce an array. These values are then fed into a final dense layer that outputs the log- wavefunction coefficients for each photon number in a multi-head fashion.

The value chosen for the parameter α of the modified Hamiltonian in Eq. 6 is the av- erage photon number of the mean-field ground state.
